Ballantyne, G.R. and Powell, M.S. (2014). Benchmarking comminution energy consumption for the processing of copper and gold ores. Minerals Engineering, 65, 109-114. doi:10.1016/j.mineng.2014.05.017

Locators are printed page numbers (109-114). A survey/benchmarking paper: nearly all results are in figures (cost-curve style bar charts) with no printed per-mine numbers, so only the printed text averages were loaded: comminution electricity per tonne of copper (1134 kWh/t) and per ounce of gold (353 kWh/oz), plus the 1975 Battelle comparison values (3410 kWh/t Cu, 42.9 kWh/oz Au; reprinted). These are per unit of FINAL METAL, not per tonne of ore or per circuit stage, so they do not map to an archetype (no kWh/t-ore stage values are printed). Chart-read values, Fig. 6-10 and Table 1 normalisation factors were not loaded. Copper-equivalent and total-energy-cost figures are in other-values. No costs, no capex, no flows or measures.
